A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of DMD and LGMD2D is not always easy to make, but the clinical, biochemical, immunohistochemical and genetic data can help to distinguish between them.
the diagnosis of DMD and LGMD2D can be very difficult in patients with high CK, and a normal molecular genetic test for DMD.
the molecular genetic testing is essential for accurate and timely diagnosis and that it is necessary for a genetic counseling of the patients and their families.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a muscle biopsy should be done in all patients with a high level of creatine kinase, even in the absence of a family history of muscular dystrophy.
the diagnosis of LGMD should be considered in patients with high level of CK, dystrophic features and absence of mutations in the dystrophin gene.
